requirement: State-changing endpoints (POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE) that rely on cookie-based session authentication must require a CSRF token or an equivalent double-submit/custom-header check.
prohibited: A state-changing endpoint that authenticates purely via an automatically-sent session cookie, with no CSRF token or custom-header verification.
remediation: Add CSRF token middleware (e.g. csurf-equivalent) to all cookie-session-authenticated state-changing routes, and have the frontend send the token on every such request.

requirement: Session/authentication cookies must set SameSite=Strict or SameSite=Lax, unless a documented cross-site use case requires SameSite=None (which must then also set Secure).
prohibited: Setting a session/auth cookie with no SameSite attribute, or SameSite=None without Secure.
good_example: res.cookie('session', token, { sameSite: 'Strict', secure: true, httpOnly: true });
remediation: Set SameSite=Strict or Lax on all session cookies; use None+Secure only where a documented cross-site requirement exists.

requirement: GET endpoints must be side-effect-free (read-only). Any endpoint that changes state must use POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE.
prohibited: A GET endpoint that performs a state-changing action (e.g. deleting a resource, modifying data) purely because it's reachable via a simple link/image tag.
remediation: Move the state-changing logic to a POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE endpoint with CSRF protection; GET must remain read-only.
